rendered: The document does not say that the EG process corroded the aluminium foil. It reports the opposite: the EG separation fully recovered the foils with shiny surfaces. The foil was fully recovered without any corrosion, and the foil surfaces showed no corrosion.[1][2][3] The XRD pattern of the recovered foil matched only aluminium, so the process was judged not to corrode the aluminium.[4] The general reason the document gives for the risk of corrosion is that aluminium foils are reactive and easily corroded during separation, which can contaminate the active materials.[5][6] The mechanism the document actually describes is for water, which it rejects as a delamination solvent: lithium leaching from the NMC cathode made the water solution basic and corroded the foil.[7][8] The corrosion would contaminate the NMC particles because it forms aluminium hydroxide precipitates on the cathode surfaces.[9] How any corrosion product would be removed is not described. The document only says the delaminated cathode was rinsed with alcohol to remove EG residues, and the foil was recovered clean without corrosion.[10][11]
